## General CAP/DA eligibility criteria
Medicaid covers CAP/DA when the beneficiary:

- **Meets the required HCBS nursing facility level of care (LOC)** as determined by NC Medicaid, and needs long-term care support at a level typically provided in an institution, tied to a documented medical diagnosis and functional care need, as assessed quarterly.
- Has a CAP assessment showing a **reasonable indication** that the person would need at least one CAP/DA HCBS service within **30 calendar days** of the evaluation.

- Is **able to maintain health, safety, and well-being** in the primary private residence or an approved location with formal and informal supports.
- Has paid care needs that can be maintained **within the average institutional cost** of the CAP/DA waiver.
- Has a **primary physician** who can link and coordinate all medical services.
- Has an **emergency back-up and disaster plan** specifying who will provide care if key direct care staff cannot provide services, if the primary caregiver has an emergency, or during a public health emergency such as a weather event or pandemic.

The policy says Medicaid covers **Consumer-Directed services** only if the beneficiary meets **all of the above** plus these additional requirements:

- **Understands the rights and responsibilities** of directing their own care, shown by completion of a mandatory self-assessment questionnaire and introductory consumer direction training and orientation.
- Is **willing and emotionally capable** of taking on employer responsibilities under consumer-directed care, or chooses a representative who is willing and capable to direct the care.
- Meets the specific criteria listed in **Subsection 3.2.2(a) and (b)**.
- Has an **approved service plan** identifying the amount, duration, frequency, and NPI of CAP/DA and non-CAP/DA services, approved by the Case Management Entity (CME).
- Receives services according to all requirements in the policy and all applicable federal and state laws, rules, regulations, standards of practice, and provider policies.
- Signs and follows the **Beneficiary Rights and Responsibilities** agreement.

## NC Medicaid Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Criteria

### 1) Entrance Criteria
A beneficiary meets entrance criteria if all of the following are present:

- A current **DSM-5** diagnosis (or any subsequent edition of that reference material)

- If a higher level of care is indicated but unavailable, or the beneficiary is refusing that service, outpatient services can be provided until the appropriate level of care is available or to support participation in that higher level of care

### 2) Continued Service Criteria
Continued services are supported if **any one** of the following is true:

- The desired outcome or level of functioning has **not been restored, improved, or sustained** over the timeframe in the treatment plan
- The beneficiary **continues to be at risk for relapse** based on current clinical assessment and history
- The gains are of a **tenuous nature**

And, in addition, **any one** of the following must also be true:

- The beneficiary has achieved current treatment plan goals, and **additional goals are indicated** as evidenced by documented symptoms; or

- The beneficiary’s level of functioning has **improved with respect to the goals outlined in the treatment plan**
- The beneficiary or legally responsible person **no longer wishes to receive these services**
- The beneficiary, based on presentation and **failure to show improvement despite modifications in the treatment plan**, requires a more appropriate best practice or evidence-based treatment modality based on North Carolina community practice standards

The federal regulation says CMS will not grant the waiver unless the state gives the required assurances and documentation. The key items I found are:

### 1) Required assurances and supporting documentation
A waiver request must include:
- the assurances required by **§ 441.302**, and
- supporting documentation required by **§ 441.303**.  
Section ID: **sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-441:441.301**

### 2) Person-centered service plan and eligibility structure
If the state furnishes HCBS under the waiver, the request must provide that services are furnished:
- under a **written person-centered service plan** approved by the Medicaid agency;
- only to beneficiaries **not inpatients** of a hospital, NF, or ICF/IID; and
- only to beneficiaries whom the agency determines would, without these services, require the Medicaid-covered level of care provided in a hospital, nursing facility, or ICF/IID.  
Section ID: **sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-441:441.301**

### 3) Scope of the waiver request
The request must:
- describe qualifications of the individual(s) who develop the plan of care;
- describe the group(s) of individuals to whom services will be offered;
- describe each service separately; and
- be limited to one or more of the permitted target groups.  
Section ID: **sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-441:441.301**

### 4) State assurances under § 441.302
CMS requires assurances on:
- **Health and welfare** — necessary safeguards to protect beneficiaries;
- **Financial accountability** — assurance the state will account for waiver funds;
- **Administrative authority** — the state must retain and exercise authority;
- **Qualified providers** — providers must meet applicable qualifications;
- **Service plan** — beneficiaries must receive services under a person-centered plan;
- **Evaluation/reassessment** and other oversight requirements.
